interest: Shows Allied friction over exporting Japan's stockpiled rubber, tin and antimony versus restitution, plus 1945–46 import statistics.
overview: This file covers diplomatic correspondence and official reporting regarding the trade, import, and raw material disposition policies of occupied Japan following the Second World War. The primary documents consist of a February 1946 diplomatic communication from Assistant Secretary of State William L. Clayton to French Ambassador Henri Bonnet concerning the export and legal status of Japanese stockpiles of rubber, tin, and antimony, as well as a proposed Inter-Allied Supply Committee; a February 1947 airgram from the U.S. Embassy in London transmitting figures given in the British House of Commons regarding raw materials imported into Japan between September 1945 and October 1946; and an archival chargeout slip from the 1980s.

subfiles.about: Diplomatic communication regarding U.S. proposals to export Japanese stockpiles of rubber, tin, and antimony to fund essential imports, and addressing French inquiries on looted materials.
subfiles.summary: William L. Clayton tells French Ambassador Henri Bonnet the U.S. plans to export half of Japan's rubber, tin and antimony stocks to fund imports, while agreeing to examine whether any were looted.
subfiles.title: Diplomatic Note from William L. Clayton to Henri Bonnet Regarding Japanese Stockpiles of Raw Materials

subfiles.about: Airgram forwarding a British parliamentary question and answer outlining the tonnage and sources of raw materials imported into Japan from September 1945 to October 1946.
subfiles.summary: Airgram from London reporting Hector McNeill's February 18, 1947 Commons answer on Japan's imports from September 1945 to October 1946, including U.S. cotton and petroleum and Chinese salt.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-335 from London Transmitting House of Commons Statement on Japanese Raw Material Imports
